doc.title: Walter Booker and Jimmy Cobb interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995

title: Coltrane in the line from Hawkins, Lester Young and Parker
summary: Asked about Coltrane, Cobb places him in a line of innovators from Coleman Hawkins to Lester Young and Parker.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: I want to ask you for a moment I just have to include this. Tell us about, a little bit anyhow, about John Coltrane, one of the most revered musicians who has ever lived, one of the most imitated saxophone players by everybody who’s ever tried to play a tenor.

Well you know it’s the same thing as what happened with — it’s a person like that comes maybe every so often, you know, that really changes the whole thing around. Like a long time ago I remember, you know, from where I’m starting, I’m starting like from maybe from Coleman Hawkins. But I’m sure there was people that influenced him, the way he played you know. Then after Coleman Hawkins it went into like Lester Young, which was a different style you know. Everybody thought that Lester Young was supposed to play like Coleman Hawkins. In fact somebody told me that his landlord told him, say, “I don’t know what kind of music you’re playing, you’re supposed to play, listen to this, this is the way you’re supposed to play the saxophone.” And had him listen to Coleman Hawkins, you know.
